prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: land/coastal/cryosphere products; predictable latency/documented quality; ground excludes spacecraft/launch/external-processing except interfaces. Mission Control Center(Bluebell): supervision/planning/authorized-command release; coordinates processing-impacting changes with Payload Processing Facility(Forgehouse); sends anomaly/outage/configuration constraints→Mission Planning System(Cedar), authoritative timeline/contact planner. User Services Portal/internal channels→observation requests; Portal records acceptance/review. Admission checks authority/target/timing/mode/volume/restrictions. Cedar→draft schedule/Contact booking requests; covers imaging/recorder/housekeeping/S-band support/high-volume X-band opportunities; flags spacecraft/station/staffing conflicts; checks slew/sun-angle/power/thermal-recovery/recorder/command-load/incompatible-activity separation. Flight Dynamics Facility(Mistral)→orbit/maneuver/visibility/pointing predictions. Flight Dynamics Team→Mistral tracking/validated timestamps; reviews uncertainty/geometry margins; coordinates orbit-control/attitude/tracking/post-burn with Spacecraft Operations Team. Payload Calibration Team reviews calibration/resource/configuration conflicts; sends approved Calibration Patch Bundle. Cedar→Forgehouse planning metadata(not product commitment); Primary Processing Cluster/Backup Processing Cluster considered only for routine-capacity compatibility. Ground Network Manager(Juniper): assignments/availability/conflicts/maintenance/staffing/site coordination; Antenna Deicing Notice→Spacecraft Operations Team contingency-margin assessment; confirms maintenance compatibility before command-preparation release; pins threatened critical paths. Converged Cedar→command preparation package→Bluebell command engineering. Command Validation Gateway(Osprey): mandatory independent preapproval/uplink barrier; checks syntax/timing/ranges/sequencing/mode/approved-baseline; rejects unauthorized edits/missing provenance/expired configuration/outside-authority-window activities. Telemetry Ingest Service: frames→continuity/framing/metadata→operations/engineering/processing; latest state→command-assumption checks; produces Pass Replay Packet. Orbit Determination Engine: tracking→orbital solution/state/predictions/Doppler Residual Report; confirms time-tags/visibility/attitude geometry. Product Quality Service: predissemination checks; geometry/mode planning feedback. Network Control System(Lantern): authoritative circuits/routes/allocation/status; receives Bluebell prepass readiness. Bluebell validates timing alarms before operations notification. North S-Band Antenna/South S-Band Antenna→commands/low-rate telemetry→Bluebell/protected routers; Kiruna X-Band

New part:
S125: The Cybersecurity Desk reviews command preparation exceptions when unusual access, emergency procedure use, or nonstandard transfer paths are requested before uplink.
S126: Final approval requires concurrence from the Mission Control Center and the Spacecraft Operations Team before any command stack is placed in the queue for the next authorized uplink opportunity.
S127: After final command approval, orbit state management remains under continuous control so that operations users work from a common predicted trajectory.
S128: The Orbit Determination Engine fits dynamic orbit solutions using radiometric tracking, spacecraft telemetry timing, force models, and the latest approved maneuver history.
S129: Tracking arcs include measurements associated with the North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna when those data meet quality and timing criteria.
S130: The Product Quality Service checks each orbit solution for frame consistency, covariance reasonableness, time-tag continuity, and agreement with recent contact predictions.
S131: The Flight Dynamics Team uses the residual report to separate station-related tracking biases from dynamic model errors before accepting an orbit solution.
S132: The Flight Dynamics Facility maintains the authoritative orbit catalog for the ground segment and records the modeling assumptions applied to each accepted solution.
S133: Maneuver screening evaluates orbit maintenance options against fuel use, ground contact visibility, payload outage constraints, and post-burn tracking opportunities.
S134: For each candidate burn, the Flight Dynamics Team computes expected state change, execution tolerance, recovery strategy, and the earliest time when the solution can be declared stable.
S135: Collision assessment uses externally supplied conjunction data together with the current covariance to estimate miss distance, encounter geometry, and probability of collision.
S136: The Flight Dynamics Team maintains screening rules that distinguish routine catalog monitoring from events requiring immediate operator notification.
S137: If the predicted risk exceeds the mission threshold, the Spacecraft Operations Team receives a maneuver recommendation package that includes timing constraints and operational impacts.
S138: Attitude geometry support translates the predicted orbit into Sun angle, Earth limb, lunar exclusion, target visibility, and antenna pointing information for daily operations.
S139: The Flight Dynamics Facility sends the Star Tracker Mask File after verifying predicted bright-object exclusions against the current attitude plan.
S140: Bluebell requires that each flight dynamics delivery include a validity interval, coordinate frame, generation time, and operational use statement.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
